svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.10.19.3 Location of Smoke Alarms
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.10.19.3 Location of Smoke Alarms
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Location of Smoke Alarms

g.text: Smoke alarm, shown on the plan. Tags: a = Clause (1)(a), i = in each sleeping room (bedroom), ii = hallway
At least one smoke alarm on each storey, including basements.
Storey with sleeping rooms: one in each sleeping room, and one between the sleeping rooms and
the remainder of the storey, in the hallway where the sleeping rooms are served by a hallway.
Installed to CAN/ULC-S553, on or near the ceiling.
The plans show one storey each, laid side by side. Interconnection is in 9.10.19.5.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Within dwelling units, sufficient smoke alarms
are installed so that there is at least one smoke
alarm installed on each storey, including
basements
And on any storey containing sleeping rooms, a smoke
alarm is installed (i) in each sleeping room, and
(ii) in a location between the sleeping rooms and
the remainder of the storey, and if the sleeping
rooms are served by a hallway, in the hallway. See
A smoke alarm required by Sentence (1) is
installed in conformance with CAN/ULC-S553
"Standard for the Installation of Smoke Alarms."
Smoke alarms required in Article 9.10.19.1. and
Sentence (1) are installed on or near the ceiling
The living area is the most frequent point of origin
of fires in dwelling units, and the main concern is
warning people asleep in bedrooms. Where a choice
arises, an alarm should be as close as possible to a
living area, while meeting the bedroom requirements.
A split-level dwelling unit needs one per storey,
not one per level.
Drawn: one dwelling unit, three storeys as plans with walls cut low. Layout is illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.19.3. (page 9-98), with Note A-9.10.19.3.(1)
